teaser: Put your customer on your Wardley map. Google and Amazon moved theirs to commodity and lost trust; airports moved back. Local delivery should be infrastructure.
core_idea: Where a company places its customer on the Wardley evolution axis shapes how it treats them; dominant platforms drift customers towards commodity, losing trust in ways price-based monopoly tests miss, while airports show the opposite loop, and local fulfilment treated as public infrastructure would open room for founders.

figures.caption: Where does your customer sit on your map? Along the evolution axis of a Wardley map: custom built, a customer you know and care for; product, a customer you sell to; commodity, a customer you do not care about. Arrows show the drift, as I see it: search users and shoppers moved right as ads became the purpose, and so did social media users; airport passengers moved back left, once better service made them spend more.
